extracted.intended_audience: university communications staff and researchers preparing research press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting, reviewing, approving, timing, and distributing university research press releases so they are newsworthy, accurate, and media-ready.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length and format
rubrics_metrics.description: 300-500 words (one page); maximum 800 words; shorter releases more likely read and used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the release concise — aim for a one-page release in the 300–500 word range; 800 words is the hard maximum. Shorter releases are more likely to be read and used by media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead with what matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Open the release with the research impact or innovation and the most important facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with research impact/innovation, relevant data and statistics, connection to broader trends or national conversation, unique attributes ("firsts," "largest," etc.), and broader implications that make the story compelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Include appropriate quotes from institutional and research voices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer quotes from key administrators, lead researchers, co-authors (if collaborative), and independent experts where possible. Ensure quoted individuals approve their quotes before distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone (objective and plain language)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an objective tone and plain language; avoid promotional language and jargon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate technical terms into everyday language, avoid marketing-speak, and write in a way that non-specialists can understand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field importance / Newsworthiness in field
rubrics_metrics.description: The research represents a major contribution to its field (new discovery, methodological advancement, replication, refutation, first time something done).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize why peers in the field would consider the work important — novelty, methodological improvements, replication of key findings, or overturning prior thinking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public impact / Public impact clear
rubrics_metrics.description: The research has clear implications for the public (affects lives, changes understanding, practical applications, health/environmental relevance, personal relatability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spell out how the work matters to people outside the field: technologies or breakthroughs that could affect lives, health implications, environmental relevance, or relatable human impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explainability
rubrics_metrics.description: The research can be explained without specialist knowledge and has a visual or memorable story angle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose findings that can be made understandable to general audiences, use visuals where helpful, and identify a clear story angle reporters can use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and approval before distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain approvals from supervisor and communications office and other stakeholders before releasing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications office review is required; legal review for sensitive topics; quoted individuals must approve their quotes; partner organizations should sign off. Build a 3–5 business day review window into scheduling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required institutional approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Secure approvals from relevant institutional offices as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depending on content, obtain sign-off from the research integrity office (for sensitive findings), IP/tech transfer (if patentable), funding agencies (if required), co-investigators, and industry partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution timing for future events
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribute releases 1–2 weeks before future events when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For upcoming events or launches, issue the release 1–2 weeks in advance to allow media planning and attendance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution timing for past events/achievements
rubrics_metrics.description: Issue releases within 24–48 hours of a past event or achievement — while newsworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness matters: for recent accomplishments or events, send the release within 1–2 days while media interest is current.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo coordination and management
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate and respect journal embargoes when the release is tied to a journal article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align timing with the journal embargo, distribute under embargo to selected media as appropriate, and lift the embargo when the journal publishes. Ensure correct embargo timing to avoid media missteps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding source acknowledged
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge funders and comply with funder acknowledgment requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include funder names and any required wording; missing funder acknowledgment is a common failure and may breach funding requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite peer-reviewed publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference and cite the peer-reviewed publication associated with the research when available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide citation details and links to the journal article where possible to allow reporters to verify and read the source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia provided
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide multimedia assets to accompany the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer images, video, figures, or other visual materials to make the story more usable for media; the absence of multimedia reduces pick-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researcher availability for interview
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure researchers are available for media interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List contact information and confirm that lead researchers can speak to the press; lack of available spokespeople hampers coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate caveats and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Include proper caveats and note limitations of the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State limitations, avoid overclaiming, distinguish correlation from causation, and clarify preclinical vs. clinical implications where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish correlation vs causation
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly avoid implying causation when only correlations are shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state whether findings are observational/correlational and avoid headlines or text that overstate causal claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish preclinical vs clinical
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify whether results are preclinical (e.g., animal/lab) or clinical (human).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid extrapolating animal or lab results to humans without appropriate caveats; label the research stage clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note study limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly note the study's limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include any sample-size, generalizability, methodological, or other constraints so media can accurately convey the findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lab affiliation correct
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure lab and institutional affiliations are accurately stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double-check institutional and lab names to avoid errors that can undermine credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-authors acknowledged
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge co-authors and collaborators appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List co-authors or provide direction on where reporter can find full author lists (e.g., the paper).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with funding agency requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow any reporting or wording requirements imposed by funding agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the release meets agency rules about acknowledgement, embargoes, or disclaimers to avoid compliance issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: AP style throughout
rubrics_metrics.description: Write the release using Associated Press (AP) style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use AP style for consistency and newsroom compatibility (dates, numbers, titles, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overhype/"breakthrough" without basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not label findings as a 'breakthrough' or overhype results beyond what the evidence supports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist sensational claims; overstatement damages credibility and is a common failure noted in releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid animal-to-human extrapolation without caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not imply animal or preclinical results directly translate to humans without clear caveats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state when work is preclinical and avoid making clinical promises based on animal data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid burying the actor (clear attribution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not bury the actor — clearly state who did the work and who is speaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use active phrasing where possible and ensure the lead actor (researcher, institution) is named early rather than obscured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid marketing-speak
rubrics_metrics.description: Refrain from using promotional or marketing language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the release factual and news-focused rather than resembling a product marketing blurb.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide researcher contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Include contact details so reporters can reach researchers for follow-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List phone/email and availability; missing researcher contact is a frequent reason a release fails to generate coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid internal jargon
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use institution-specific or technical jargon that general audiences won't understand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate or define necessary technical terms; internal shorthand should be removed or explained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct embargo timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure embargo times are accurate and communicated clearly to media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mistimed or incorrectly communicated embargoes can result in lost coverage or journal conflicts; coordinate closely with journals and partners.
